STIPULATION MARKUP ANALYSIS - Hargrove Capital Partners LLC v. Commissioner, Dkt. 8341-23 (privileged work product)
To: K. Ellsworth. Re: Respondent's 12/6/2024 markup vs. our 11/1/2024 served draft (147 paras). Deadlines: call offered 12/17-19; stipulation 1/15/2025; trial 4/14/2025.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Do not sign. (a) The markup is not a true redline of what we served: numbering and text diverge from para. 1 on, so unmarked changes exist, and the cover letter's counts (34 modified/8 deleted/12 added) do not match the markup's own index (about 18 modified, 5 deleted, 12 added). (b) Six changes are substantive and must be rejected: ownership (para. 22), GP purpose (38), "unified plan" (47), ClearView date (78/83/139), valuation inputs (90-93), reliance (112). (c) Deletions of the 9/15/2016 minutes (62-65) and the Appeals paragraph (118) need a counter, not a flat concession. (d) New paras. 148-158 largely feed a 707(a)(2)(A) theory not developed in the SNOD. (e) Our own draft has errors we must fix before negotiating (Section 5). Strategy: demand a Word-compare, treat unmarked variances as rejected, negotiate agreed and disputed-with-reservation sections.

2. PRIORITIZED ISSUES (Critical first)
C1. Para. 22 - ownership 87.5% changed to 92.3%. Rejected. LPA Schedule A Part III (and Part IV for GP V) shows Hargrove 87.5%, Rachel M. Hargrove (spouse) 7.5%, Hargrove Family Trust 5.0%, unchanged since formation. IRS cites unidentified "K-1s." Impact: 4.8 points x about $43.2M of carry is roughly $2.07M more income to Derek, about $386K more tax on the SNOD's $8.05M rate/NIIT base, plus penalty. Demand the K-1s. The 12.5% is NOT "other senior investment professionals" (our served para. 22, markup para. 23, the Thornfield opinion, and our case memo all say so). Correct it; it also removes the memo's "shared ownership" strength and invites related-person questions. Fund V LPA was not in the file; confirm GP V Schedule A.

C2. Para. 47 - "unified investment plan" replaced by "separate and distinct"; IRS calls it a legal conclusion contradicted by the record. Reject. Record: 9/15/2016 minutes state the committee "discussed that the initial $13.3 million investment and the anticipated $7 to $10 million in follow-on capital should be viewed as components of a single, integrated investment plan," resolved to reserve $7-10M for 18-24 months, and the base case assumed an add-on; LPA s.3.3(a),(c),(d) makes follow-ons "authorized and expected," aggregates initial and follow-on investments for cost and returns, and Amendment No. 1 (3/1/2018, 66-2/3% LP consent) raised the reserve to 18% expressly for MidSouth. Counter: neutral facts - quote the minutes, s.3.3, Amendment 1, amounts and timing ($8.2M within range; about 18 months), and stipulate the parties dispute characterization (kept in IRS para. 70). Caveats: the resolution makes each deployment "subject to future Investment Committee approval" (IRS will use; IC approval date 3/8/2018 in markup para. 53 vs 2/28/2018 in served para. 65 - verify). Even aggregated, the holding period is 1,047 days (about 2y10.5m), short of three years, so this theory alone does not defeat 1061; its value is tranche allocation and penalty reasonableness.

C3. Para. 112 - "relied in good faith" cut to "received." Counter, do not concede. Good faith is mixed fact/law, but Rule 91 requires stipulating facts not fairly disputable; reliance elements are facts (Neonatology Assocs. v. Commissioner, 115 T.C. 43 (2000), aff'd 299 F.3d 221 (3d Cir. 2002), from memory, not re-verified). Propose: Hargrove requested the opinions, reviewed and discussed them with Nakamura before filing (paras. 113-114, 119 survive in the markup), the returns followed them, and he emailed that he would follow the recommended position. Reserve "good faith." Risks to resolve before stipulating Exhibits 18-19: the 3/15/2020 opinion cites Prop. Reg. s.1.1061-4, but the proposed regulations were published 8/14/2020 (T.D. 9945 final 1/19/2021), and it refers to a "March 10, 2021" opinion a year ahead - indicating later revision or backdating; it concedes its single-plan result is still about six weeks short and rests on an admittedly "aggressive" partner-level holding period argument (statute substitutes 3 years for 1 year in s.1222, applied to asset holding periods); Nakamura both prepared the returns and attended the 9/15/2016 IC (advisor independence). Get native files/metadata first; 2021 opinion not supplied.

C4. Paras. 78, 83, 139 - ClearView closing 11/8/2017 changed to 12/12/2017 (965 to 931 days; Ex. 9 date). Reject. Our file shows four consistent sources: executed purchase agreement, closing binder, Blackpine wire, and 10/25/2017 capital call notice. IRS says its executed purchase agreement shows 12/12/2017; demand its copy. Impact is limited: both dates give under three years and precede 12/22/2017 enactment; 1061 applies to tax years beginning after 12/31/2017 with no pre-enactment grandfathering in the statute, so the memo's "pre-TCJA cushion/transitional" argument is weak. Still reject (accuracy, exhibit integrity).

C5. Paras. 89-93 - valuation inputs rewritten (WACC 12.5% to 14.8%; growth 3.0% to 2.0%; multiple 8.5x to 7.2x; 3/15/2018 value $38.4M to $31.7M; "primary" to "one of"). Reject paras. 90-93. A stipulation must state what Ridgecrest did; IRS inputs are expert opinion/contention (served para. 126: IRS expert report was due 12/15/2024 - demand it). Ridgecrest's executive summary (10/15/2019) uses exactly 12.5%/3.0%/8.5x, weights DCF 60%/GPC 40%, and its sensitivity table shows IRS's three inputs together cut 3/15/2018 enterprise value from $119.7M to $105.4M (-11.9%); neither $38.4M nor $31.7M appears (concluded equity value $101.5M). Lower 3/15/2018 value shifts gain to the follow-on tranche.

C6. Para. 38 - GP purpose changed to "primary purpose of receiving carried interest." Reject. LPA "General Partner Purpose" and s.5.1: formed to serve as general partner; carry is allocated "in its capacity as a partner" (s.7.1). The change feeds 707(a)(2)(A).

I1. Paras. 62-65 deleted; para. 118 deleted. Minutes: IRS refuses authenticity "subject to foundation" yet does not deny them; its own markup (para. 52, 62) and the exam record likely include them. Counter: stipulate authenticity and existence/content as business records (FRE 803(6), 902(11)), reserving relevance; else call Leung (recorder) or Hargrove, and use Rule 91(f). The deleted text shown by IRS (e.g., 9/12/2016 memo naming "three" targets) does not match our served paras. 62-65 or the minutes (two targets) - challenge. Para. 118: Appeals "merit" statements are likely inadmissible under FRE 408 (applied in Tax Court via Rule 143) and do not bind the Commissioner; our served version adds quotes ("compelling," "inclined to concede") our memo does not source. Concede para. 118 only for movement on C2/C3; keep para. 30.

I2. Para. 85 - new Petitioner "contention" that holding period "exceeds 3 years" and credit-facility draws extend it. Not ours; contradicts served paras. 142-143 and our memo (under 3 years). Reject; restore served contention paras.

I3. Silent/unflagged changes (examples; full compare required): (i) markup para. 31 "Augst" correction inserts a new fact - audit commenced "August 5, 2019" (MidSouth's sale date; audit began 1/18/2021, para. 26); (ii) para. 28 says Stonebridge prepared the protest (served para. 107: Thornfield; we were engaged 4/5/2023, para. 128); (iii) para. 120 places Ellsworth and "James R. Whitfield" at Appeals (served para. 108: Muñoz, Nakamura, Hargrove) - false and reliance-relevant; (iv) paras. 18-19 carry to HCP and fees "from Fund IV and V" (served: carry to GP entities; fees from funds; our memo says Funds III-IV-V) - reconcile; (v) paras. 21 and 42 "sole authority/sole discretion" vs LPA s.5.3 (majority IC vote including chairman) and served para. 39 - feeds services narrative; (vii) paras. 52-53 IC members "Tanaka/Andrea Reeves" vs minutes (Hargrove, Wilder, Samantha Reeves); (viii) paras. 8, 9, 55 HQs and footprint (14 centers/six states vs Ridgecrest six centers in TX/OK/LA/AR; HQ varies across five documents); (ix) para. 57 $4.3M escrow; (xi) paras. 14 and 1-3 add home address and full EINs - Tax Court Rule 27 privacy redaction (verify); (xii) silent omission of served paras. 36-37, 59-61, 64-70, 120, 134-146 (board and 2/28/2018 minutes, contentions); (xiii) preamble: "binding for all purposes" and "admissible without foundation" - Rule 91(e) limits effect to this case; objections reserved.

I4. New paras. 148-158 (Respondent's 12 adds, incl. reservation 159).
- 148-149 (65%/35% time; services): from IDR 7 records "produced by Petitioner"; our memo says time is not bifurcable. Verify against production; relevance low since we conceded API status (served para. 138). Reject percentages; accept para. 149 reworded.
- 150 (no salary): verify returns/K-1s; qualify.
- 151 (carry terms not arm's-length): reject; LPs institutional, advisory committee negotiated terms (served para. 28), 66-2/3% LP consent to Amendment 1.
- 152 (fee offset): truncated and mis-cited (s.8.3 is organizational expenses; offset is s.8.2 - our served paras. 28-29 repeat the error). Substitute LPA s.8.2(a)-(c): offset only to extent carry exceeds cumulative fees, one-directional, no recharacterization, fee and carry separate capacities.
- 153-154: verify amounts to Forms 1065 (4.8+3.9+5.1+4.8 = 18.6 arithmetic is right; LPA s.8.1(c) says $18.6M is Fund IV+V). Reject 154 ($61.8M "economic benefit"): argumentative, mixes recipients.
- 155-156 (Fund III $14.3M "not challenged"; identical terms): irrelevant (different year/pre-1061; no estoppel); double-edged. Reject, or accept with relevance reserved.
- 157 (no written policy): true (Thornfield; Interrogatory 14) - accept, but strike "or contemplating" and add s.3.3, Amendment 1, minutes.
- 158 ("3 of 11" companies): conflicts with served paras. 33-34 (6 + 8 = 14); reject until reconciled.
Burden: 707(a)(2)(A) appears only secondarily in the 30-day letter/Appeals; new matter or increased deficiency carries Respondent's burden (Rule 142(a)). Do not stipulate facts for an unpleaded theory; ask about an amended answer.

I5. Penalty. Add facts on 6662(b) basis (markup para. 34) and supervisory approval under 6751(b): markup para. 123 identifies SRA Robert Chen's review; seek stipulation of the date/form of written approval of the initial penalty determination and 7491(c) production burden.

I6. $38.7M does not reconcile. SNOD: $38.7M recharacterized. Tranche theory described in our memo: 38.1% x $26.4M = $10.06M + $16.8M ClearView = $26.9M; $38.7M implies 83% of MidSouth carry. Also NIIT of $1,470,600 is stated as caused by recharacterization although 1411 applies to capital gain and ordinary investment income alike; and "entity-level" income tax on pass-throughs is odd under BBA. Do not stipulate para. 32's causal wording or that the IRS's "position" is tranche-only (para. 69); request IRS computation. LPA s.7.1 is whole-fund: $26.4M carry is 57% of $46.3M gross profit, so pro-rating carry by tranche is questionable.

3. COVER LETTER POINTS
Letter attributes date/ownership/valuation "corrections" to exam records without producing them: request them. Threatened Rule 91(f) motion and "separate statement of contested facts": 91(f) motions are due 45 days before the trial calendar call (about 2/28/2025 - confirm in current Rules/standing order); we can use it too.

4. RECOMMENDATIONS / NEXT STEPS
1. By 12/10: written demand for Word-compare against the 11/1 draft, IRS "records" (ClearView agreement, K-1s showing 92.3%, IDR 7 time records, Interrogatory 14), IRS expert report, penalty approval form.
2. Take 12/17-19 call; agenda: accept typos/date format/Rule 91 cite/para. 157 (revised)/149/152 (our text); hold on C1-C6.
3. Internal by 12/13: correct our draft (Section 5); pull Exs. 4-A, 6-A, Blackpine wires, LPA V, GP operating agreements, Thornfield native files; prepare Hargrove/Nakamura/Leung/Callahan for authentication and cross.
4. Counter-draft by 12/20 with Part A (agreed), Part B (disputed, each side's version, objections reserved); finalize before 1/15/2025; calendar 91(f).
5. Reassess merits: partner-level and grandfathering theories are weak; weight penalty defense.

5. ERRORS IN OUR OWN DRAFT (fix before negotiating)
Served para. 22/23 (12.5% holders); 27 (pref return non-compounded per LPA s.7.1(b); catch-up is 100% to GP); 28-29 (s.8.2); 31 (Fund IV commitments $350M, closings 6/15, 9/30, 12/15/2015, not $225M/8/15); 36 (s.3.3, 18%); 40/59 (three voting IC members); 45, 50, 86-87, 93, 97 (MidSouth revenue $89M/EBITDA $12.7M per minutes vs $78M/$9.8M per Ridgecrest vs $48M/$7.2M; Fund IV owned about 19.4% at entry and about 50% at sale, not 100%; Ridgecrest report dated 10/15/2019 about 185 pages, "litigation support," Callahan 18 years - not 4/30/2019, 87 pages; concluded EVs $80.1M/$119.7M/$158.0M; also entry EV $52M/4.1x in minutes vs $80.1M - prepare for IRS exploitation); GP IV operating agreement date (5/28/2015) precedes formation (6/8/2015); "tax matters partner" should read partnership representative post-BBA.
Unresolved: BBA procedure for entity-level adjustments; Fund V documents not supplied; true source of 92.3%.
